where: Exam traps, fourth trap (sin α cos α)
problem: The direction of the error is stated backwards. In σ_t = ΔS/(t d sin α cos α) the factor sin α cos α = 0.5 sits in the denominator, so dropping it makes σ_t larger, not smaller: the wrong value is 35 000/750 = 46.7 N/mm², exactly half of the correct 93.3 N/mm². The trap claims forgetting it 'doubles σ_t', which is the opposite of what happens, and it hides that this mistake is an unsafe underestimate of the band stress.
fix: At 45° the product is 0.5, not 1, and dropping it halves σ_t (93.3 N/mm² becomes 46.7 N/mm²), an unsafe underestimate of the diagonal tension stress.

problem: The caption says the band 'passes 35 kN into the booms', but the boom node and the aria text give 52.5 kN per boom over the bay. Both numbers are right for different quantities (35 kN is the band shear ΔS; 52.5 kN is the boom axial force P = ΔS L/d with L/d = 750/500 = 1.5), but shown side by side in one figure without saying so, a student reads them as contradictory.
fix: Caption: 'The 80 kN applied shear first buckles the web at 60 N/mm²; the 45° band carries 35 kN of the shear, so 45 kN stays in the web as shear and each boom gains 52.5 kN of axial force over the 750 mm bay.'
